utterances.text: You see in the upper right-hand corner there's some handwriting up there. The English translation says: "To inform." Then it says: "CSB Doboj." And then underneath that it says: "MUP RS." And underneath that there's initials. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do. I see what it says there. I see 01. I see that it says: "Inform the Doboj CSB." And then I see that it says MUP RS. And then underneath is number 8, if I see it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: So you don't see that as a signature. Do you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handwriting is familiar. It is familiar. But I'm not sure, 01 ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this is the handwriting of Mr. Zupljanin or -- or Kesic. Or Bera. I'm not sure. Definitely a familiar handwriting, but I cannot confirm with certainty whose it is. Because the signature, if this is a signature, is not clear to me. You said it was a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this is 65 ter 20020, I believe that no nexus has been established between this witness and this document that would warranting the admission of the document into evidence. He hasn't recognised this document as being the one prepared by his group, so he cannot confirm whether this was perhaps authored by Mr. Radulovic. He explained, as far as the source was concerned, that there could have been a few people with the same pseudonym or that other operatives used the same source. Therefore, I think there's insufficient nexus between the document and this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, what is your purpose in seeking to have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, my purpose is it relates to the testimony of MS-001 at T.21142, and with regard to Mr. Aleksic's arguments, those would go to the weight of the document. You've heard some evidence that provides some authenticity to this document. It's clear that the witness could not say categorically it was or was not a report by Mr. Radulovic. But we have evidence about the source of this information as well as the possibility of the handwriting as well as the fact that it comes from the state security sector in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You said going to weight. You're seeking to have this admitted for the truth of the contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, I -- may -- yes, I'm sorry. It's just going to a couple of things. Yes, we would like it to come in for the truth of the contents. It also, because of the distribution list in the upper hand-hand corner, indicates who it was to go to which shows that these reports, regardless of who actually drafted it, made it other regions and possibly up to the RS MUP itself. So we're seeking to admit it for all those reasons. And also with regard to the substance of it, we've heard about this individual mentioned in this Official Note through several witnesses, and this corroborates some witnesses and it challenges the evidence of others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2399, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 20030, tab 48, on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While that is coming up, Mr. Olmsted, does the OTP still require time to deal with a preliminary -- a procedural matter this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The word I receive is, yes, we still need the, I think, what, 10, 15 minutes at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So you will govern yourself accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, what we have in front of us is a 9 April 1993 Official Note from the CSB Banja Luka state security sector -- oh. I don't know if I'll ever get the hang of that. Sir, what you have in front of you is a 9 April 1993 Official Note from the CSB state security sector Banja Luka. Can you take a look at this one and tell us if you can confirm that this would have been written by Mr. Radulovic and/or his team? And once you finish reading the first page, you can have a look at the second.

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next page, please. I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just for completeness, why don't we turn to the next page. There's another page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And is there a fourth page? Let's return to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Looking, sir, at the two sources named here, Partner and Cuperak, as well as the contents of this report, can you confirm that this report would have come from Mr. Radulovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning the sources that were named in paragraph 1, both of them, Mr. Prosecutor, I can tell you that I am seeing these pseudonyms for the first time. I really cannot establish any connection between them and Mr. Radulovic or our group, for that matter. I don't remember him using the sources with these pseudonyms. I went through this note quickly, and I don't know what to tell you. It seems that there is some kind of information contained in this note that I find ridiculous, if I may take the liberty of saying so. It seems that we have a person who has barely finished elementary school, though he has a thousand and seven hundred [as interpreted] people at his disposal, that he has dealings with the president of the Republic of Serbia, and I really don't know where all this information has come from. Ones again I would like to apologise if I'm being too harsh in my comments, but I really find this surprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's just turn to page 3. Do you recognise that handwriting that you have before you? It says: "Bera, modify it for the under-secretary." And then I --

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the handwriting. Both at the top and then towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the handwriting's is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First one, the upper line, is the handwriting of Mr. Nedeljko Kesic, and I see that he is suggesting to Mr. Bera that something be modified for the under-secretary. And then Mr. Bera, below, because this is his handwriting, I believe, says: "Info to the under-secretary." Which I understand to mean information to be given to the under-secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I don't want you to speculate, but is it logical to presume that the under-secretary is the under-secretary for state security at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. What am I guessing at?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speculating?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I don't want you to speculate. But it mentions an under-secretary here, and I was wondering if that would presumably mean -- the under-secretary for state security at the RS MUP level.

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. You got it right. If Mr. Kesic is writing "under-secretary," that means it must be under-secretary for national security.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And let's turn to the next page in the B/C/S. And it states: "For Zupljanin opinion." And then number 1: "I'm not sure whether there should be any mention of A. Bjelosevic." And 2: "Inform the under-secretary about the rest!" Then we see some initials at the very end of it. Can you confirm that this is Mr. Zupljanin's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The upper handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The lower handwriting. The dark handwriting, with the -- the initials right to the bottom right of it.

utterances.speaker: GORAN SAJINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the handwriting of Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to the admission of this document. First of all, the witness has not identified it either as the Official Note made by Mr. Radulovic or by himself, nor can he identify the sources. He has never heard of them. The date on the document is 9 April 1993. It has nothing to do with the incidents in the indictment. The witness also said he found it unrealistic and illogical, these references to Slobodan Milosevic and 1800 members, and I believe for all these reasons it is not fit for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one small suggestion. It was not cleared with the witness whether this handwriting can be associated with the typewritten text. I think it should have been asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Again, I don't think it's appropriate for the Stanisic Defence to be raising objections to a document seeking to tendered through a witness that's not their's. But on top of that, the witness has said that he has not personally not seen this document before, so obviously he is not going to be able to -- we don't have the paper one in front of us, but this is the complete document that I have. Your Honours, can I address the concerns raised outside the witness's presence? Because I think after that we're done with this evidence today because my colleague Ms. Korner is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So you're asking that the witness be excused at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Sajinovic, again, as was the case yesterday, we are going to ask the usher to escort you out a little ahead of us because there are a certain procedural matters with which we are to deal. We will be resuming your testimony at 2.30 tomorrow afternoon in this courtroom. There are other matters that the -- in which the Chamber is engaged before that time tomorrow. So the usher would now escort you out, and we will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry. I've heard the discussion between the Prosecutor and the gentleman from the Defence. Concerning this document I saw, the first, the second, and the third, those remarks here and the signatures I couldn't recognise because it was never the practice to use a blank sheet of paper, and all I can see here is a blank sheet of paper, to put suggestions for Mr. Zupljanin, to Mr. Bera, et cetera. As we had occasion to see on previous documents, the suggestion by the chief was written on the original note. As we saw recently, Mr. Kljuic wrote it was not for us, Mr. Zupljanin, Mr. Kesic, et cetera. I just wanted to give you this verification about this. And thank you for allowing me to say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, apart from the evidence that we previously heard plus the -- what the witness has just volunteered, casting doubt on the authenticity of this, the substantive objections is that this is a document which deals with matters outside the relevant period. So apart from those, and could you tell us why you are seeking to have this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, first of all, let me address what the witness said, and this has obviously been my concern throughout his evidence and why I've asked him, I think now a half-dozen times, to remove his earphones is, whenever he hears an objection from the other side, he voices in his opinion or view or evidence as to that issue, and I think that this -- the weight that that's entitled to, of course, Your Honours must decide, but I think that that has to be duly noted. With regard to why we were tendering this document, this witness was able to verify the handwriting. So we see that Vojin Bera is involved in this document, Nedeljko Kesic, and the accused, Stojan Zupljanin. They're all -- now, whether these handwritten notes are part of the same document or not, that's a different issue. Obviously this witness is not the one to deal with that. It also can go to weight. We can also produce the original if anyone has any questions. But unless there's any basis to contend that this document isn't what it is, which is a complete document including the handwritten notes affixed to it, I think that we're entitled to have that come in on that basis. With regard to the time-period, it is dealing with a person that has come up repeatedly in this case, Ljubisa Kitanovic. It mentions his connection with the CSB Doboj. It's clear it's from 9 April 1993, but it's clearly there is a connection between them and suggests that this was in the past. And we submit that it goes, to a certain degree, to the credibility of the evidence of MS-001, who distanced himself from this individual. And for those reasons, we think that it meets all the thresholds to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And Your Honours if I may just add, I apologise. The primary purpose I'm bringing this into evidence having not led -- or cross-examined MS-001 is it deals directly with the issue that I'm dealing with which is state security reports starting at a lower level and making it all the way up here, presumably, to the under-secretary because they're saying forward this information on to the under-secretary, and it's showing the flow of information. It's dated 1993, but these are the same individuals who were in power at CSB Banja Luka in 1992. And so it does say something about their interrelationship in the time-period relevant to this indictment. So even if the substance of the document, the crime suggested in it, do not apply to 1992, the form -- the process certainly does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please remind me: Is this the first document, confining ourselves to system and not the content of the document, is this the first document that shows the flow up to the level of the under-secretary?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I think it's the first that shows it with everybody's handwriting on it. I'm not aware of whether we have any other in evidence. None come to mind, mine or Ms. Korner's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Judge Harhoff dissenting, the document admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2400, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to keep appearing and re-appearing like a jack-in-the-box, but I am a little concerned about something that happened earlier today and the reason I'm here to deal with it is because Mr. Olmsted hasn't been in court and hasn't been dealing with these issues before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it arose at page 46, line 3 of today's transcript, again, there was an objection to the admission of a document one of the Milos group, and Mr. Krgovic got up to say this: "Your Honours, if I may raise an objection of principle. And a specific one as well. "We ask from the Prosecutor and we made a submission to this Trial Chamber that all documents concerning Mr. Zupljanin and concerning our witnesses be disclosed to us under Rule 66(B). This document fits that description. It explicitly refers to Mr. Zupljanin. But the Prosecution informed us that they have complied with this and that they have given us in August the documents in that category. This document has not been disclosed so it can't be tendered and can't be admitted." Your Honours, that is misleading in two respects. First of all, the request under Rule 66(B) which Your Honours ruled upon was specific and limited and referred to, as yet, undisclosed documents. That was the whole purpose of this, which we were proposing, or might be, and the Defence realize that, to use in cross-examination, and in light of Your Honours' ruling we complied with that. This document, Your Honour, I repeat, for the third time, and I invite Mr. Krgovic to tell us if what I am saying is wrong straight away, we had a long list of documents from the Milos group. We provided the Defence with the full list. We provided, as Mr. Olmsted said further, the full ERN numbers. We told them all these documents were on EDS. The Defence, in fact, as Mr. Olmsted has already said, came back to us and said they were unable to trace certain of these documents, and we, in fact, supplied copies of those they could not trace. Additionally, they themselves, in cross-examination of Mr. Radulovic, used some of the documents from the list that we had supplied. It is wholly and utterly misleading to say that this document was not disclosed and, in any event, fell under Rule 66(B). Now, Your Honour, before I carry on, I invite Mr. Krgovic to tell me if I am wrong in anything that I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell you, very briefly, Ms. Korner, you are wrong. Because what you said about the document being in EDS and having an ERN number, we do not consider as disclosure under 66(B). The fact that you placed it in EDS and that you said that a couple of weeks ago, is not considered proper disclosure. And when I said that the document has not been disclosed in that sense, and I will find the page of the transcript where you said that, I just didn't have time, but I do remember exactly what you said. What you said, namely, that a document with a certain number has been placed in EDS doesn't mean disclosure. Anyone who deals with this knows it's a nightmare and that's why we asked for certain documents that we couldn't find that you give us their copies because we were unable to find them in EDS. And that's the point. When I say that something has not been disclosed, proper disclosure is to give something to the Defence, the entirety of the document, rather than references or numbers. So much about that. And that's precisely the reason why we made our submission in August, asking for specific documents concerning these witnesses. And the document that I have mentioned falls under the order of the Trial Chamber and belongs to the second category of documents that should have been disclosed to the Defence, namely, and to quote from the ruling: "All reports telegrams, letters and any other documents, drafted or received by any of the Zupljanin witnesses." And the document that I pointed out falls squarely into this category because the Prosecution wanted to show that this document has been drafted and that's why it was shown to the witness. So disclosure should have been proper and clear, not in terms of a reference pertaining to EDS. That is what I meant by talking about disclosure. If the document was disclosed sometime when I was not on this case, I'm prepared to apologise before the Trial Chamber and before the OTP, but during my tenure and the entire time I've been keeping records, I have not found this document among those disclosed, and that is my explanation in response to Ms. Korner. I believe this to be a -- a rather academic discussion more than anything else, Your Honours. The document does not meet the requirements from item 15(A) of the guide-lines given by this Trial Chamber, so what Ms. Korner said also in no way responds to our second objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is not an academic discussion. The document was on the list attached to Mr. Radulovic's statement because these were the documents that were identified by him. It clearly indicates that it has Zupljanin's name on it. I have the list in front of me. It was disclosed on the 31st of July, 2009, in which case -- at which point, to my certain knowledge, Mr. Krgovic was in -- already in the case. And, as I say, it is quite inconceivable that when Mr. Radulovic gave evidence, when they asked us for specific copies, when they used other documents, that they were not aware of this list. And that is why, Your Honour, on the basis we're entitled to assume that if that's what's happened, they've had this document, it did not come under the Rule 66(B) request and never did which was to ask us to disclose documents that had not yet been disclosed. All -- the whole list, Your Honours -- and if Your Honours want to go and have a look at it, it is attached to Mr. Radulovic's composite statement. So, Your Honours, we say for the third time, and if Mr. Krgovic's record-keeping is incomplete, incompetent, or whatever, then that is not to be laid at the fault of the OTP. Your Honour, the second matter that Mr. Krgovic went on to deal with was that the Prosecution had a witness, Mr. Radulovic, who testified here, and they could have shown him that document. Your Honours, there are, as I say, over -- I think it's about 300 all together of these Milos documents. More I hear Mr. Olmsted saying. He's more familiar with that part than I am. We had a limited amount of time to deal with a very, very lengthy statement made by Mr. Radulovic. Equally in the bar table motion we had to make a selection. The Defence took the decision to call this witness - and I want to come onto the next thing that Mr. Krgovic said - and therefore we say we're entitled to put these documents to them, all of which have a been, as we say, disclosed, notwithstanding Mr. Krgovic's assertion, which I note, and I'm sorry, that he won't withdraw. Your Honours, Mr. Krgovic then went on to say: "On top of everything else -- on top of everything, the Prosecution had given up on this witness and withdrew him from the list, especially because of the wrong-doing by Mr. Koehler. This witness used to be on the Prosecution witness list and during their interviews they showed him all sorts of documents." You will note, Your Honours, that Mr. Olmsted objected at that stage. It is utterly improper to make that assertion about Mr. Koehler, and I make no bones about it, Your Honours. We will be calling Mr. Koehler to deal with these matters if these unfounded allegations persist. Indeed, Your Honours, I should say we may well be calling him in light of the allegations that are being made about him. Your Honours, finally, on this matter, and I'm sorry it is returning to what I hoped was a settled question now. When Judge Delvoie, at page 48, line 10 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner may I interrupt you and say with a phrase that is often used in this courtroom, I allow for the possibility that I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, then Your Honour, I won't take this any further. Your Honours, I'm quite happy with that. We rely on the terms of what is now the Rule 15(A), and we say that's absolutely clear. Your Honours, I'm not taking that any further, but I -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment to 2.30 tomorrow.
